caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1786 of 2011.
lawyer:
AFM Mesbahuddin, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
Md Harun-or-Rashid (In person) ------ For Respondents.
parties:
Bangladesh Technical Education Board ------ Petitioner 
VS
Md Harun-or- Rashid & others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 13-1-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 2252 of 2010)
full_judgment:
Md Muzammel Hossain CJ: This petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated 13-1-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 2252 of 2010 making the Rule absolute with a direction upon the writ respondents to transfer the writ petitioners service as computer operators to the revenue budget of the Bangladesh Technical Education Board with effect from 1-7-2005 within 2(two) months from the date of receipt of the judgment provided that the writ petitioners would not get any further salary for the period they had served on contract basis for which they had already been paid. 
2. The present respondent Nos. 1-3 as petitioners filed Writ Petition No. 2252 of 2010 before the High Court Division stating, inter alia, that the writ petitioner No. 1 passed BA Examination in the year 1996 from Gouranadi Government College, Barisal and that the writ petitioner No. 2 passed BSc Examination in the year 1998 from Sardah College, Rajshahi and the writ petitioner No. 3 passed MSc Examination in the year 2000 from Jagannath University College, Dhaka. They were appointed on 9-6-2004 as Computer Operators in the scale of Taka 4,125 (250-5505) in the Project for Computerization of Examination Activities of Bangladesh Technical Education Board (BTEB) pursuant to Notification No. বাকাশিবো/এম.আই.এস/২০০৪/১৫৩(৬) dated 9-6-2004 issued by the Bangladesh Technical Education Board. The writ petitioner Nos. 1, 2 and 3 joined on 14-6-2004, 24-6-2004 and 12-6-2004 respectively in their service. The writ petitioners continued their job till June, 2005 on the basis of the above mentioned appointment and at the end of the Project the petitioners were allowed to retain their posts as Computer Operators on contractual basis for a period of 6(six) months each time till June, 2009 vide letters dated 30-6-2005, 22-1-2006, 24-7-2006, 28-12-2006, 25-7-2007, 31-12-2008 and 22-1-2009 issued by the writ respondent No. 1 petitioner with commitment that they would be appointed to their posts on regular basis on the revenue head of the Government as soon as sanctions for the said posts is obtained from the government. The service of the writ petitioner No. 2 on contractual basis was discontinued since 25-7-2007 but he was verbally allowed to work on daily basis till June, 2009. 
3. The Ministry of Education vide Memo No. শিম/শাঃ১৬(প্রজেক্ট)৬-২-/২০০৫/(অংশ-১)/৩২ dated 30-1-2008 (Annexure-C) sanctioned 9(nine) posts of the Project for computerization of examination activities of the Board and out of the 9(nine) posts 4(four) posts were Computer Operators. The writ petitioners stated that clause 49 of the Project Profile (Annexure-D) contemplates that after the life time of the project the manpower (ten persons) of the Computerization of the project would be transferred to the revenue budget of the Board for the public interest and for continuing the computerization of examination activities in BTEB. But out of 4 sanctioned revenue posts of Computer Operators, only in one post a Computer Operator of the Project was appointed and in three other posts, persons from outside were appointed on the basis of Memo No. বাকাশিবো/প্রাঃ/০৮/২০১/২০১০/১৫২২ dated 23-2-2010 (Annexure-E) and by Memo No. বাকাশিবো/প্রাঃ/০৮/২০১/২০১০/১৫২২ dated 23-2-2010 (Annexure-G) only one post of Despatch Rider of the Board who was in service on contract basis was absorbed and appointed in the revenue posts. Thus, to the great mental shock and dismay, the writ petitioners were  illegally left out of the appointment denying them the equal treatment and frustrating their legitimate expectation for appointment to the sanctioned revenue posts pursuant to clause 49 of the Project Profile. The writ petitioners further asserted that the Notification vide SRO No. 182 /Ain/2005 Shama/Bidhi-1 /S-9/2000 dated 20-6-2005 published in Extra-ordinary Gazette dated 20-6-2005 concerning regularization and fixing seniority of the persons who have been transferred to the revenue set up from development project is not applicable in the case of the writ petitioners' service since they were appointed in the Project on 9-6-2004 prior to the publication of the said Notification and as per Rule 2(ka) of the Rules of 2005 contained by the aforesaid Notification "development project" means any project approved by the government under development budget started between 9th April, 1972 to 30th June, 1997. 
4. On 23-7-2007, 27-7-2008 and 29-7-2008 the writ respondents issued certificates of good performance [Annexure-F, F(1) and F(2)] respectively in favour of the writ petitioners and under such circumstances, having requisite qualifications, the writ petitioners rendered commendable service to the Board for a long period and that they have got legitimate expectation that they would be appointed to the vacant regular posts of Computer Operators with grade and scale as mentioned in Memo No. শিম/শাঃ১৬/বোর্ড (প্রজেক্ট)৬-২/২০০৫/(অংশ-১)/৩২ dated 30-1-2008 (Annexure-C) creating 9(nine) posts under the revenue set up of the Board. There are instances and age old practice for the Board's employees to be absorbed and appointed in permanent posts from contractual service and recently also one Md Faruque, son of Md Moinuddin Sardar, a Despatch Rider of the Board on contractual basis was absorbed and appointed to the revenue post vide Memo No. বাকাশিবো/প্রাঃ/০৮/২০১/২০১০/১৫২২ dated 23-2- 2010. The writ respondent No. 2 on 6-7-2003 issued public advertisement vide Memo No. বাকাশিবো/প্রাঃ/২০০৮/৮১২ dated 6-7-2008 inviting applications for appointment to  various permanent posts including 3(three) Computer Operators under the Board, but still now, no appointment to the permanent vacant posts of Computer Operators has been made by the Board and these posts are lying vacant with the Board. 
5. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing both parties by the impugned judgment and order dated 13-1-2011 made the Rule absolute with direction. 
6. The present petitioner being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 13-1-2011 passed by the High Court Division preferred the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before this Division. 
7. Mr AFM Mesbahuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents- petitioners submits that the High Court Division did not consider the facts that the Bangladesh Technical Education Board sent the proposal to the Ministry of Education for transfer of the writ petitioners' service to the revenue setup, but the Ministry of Establishment rejected the proposal and as such they have no authority to transfer the petitioner's service to the revenue setup. He submits that the High Court Division ignored the facts that the respondent Nos. 1-3-Writ petitioners applied for and appeared in the competency tests for direct appointment and thus they waived their right if any and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division with direction is liable to be set-aside. He further submits that the High Court Division on misconception of law relying upon clause 49 of the project profile held that the petitioners were promise bound to transfer the service of the respondent Nos. 1-3 to the revenue budget of the Board in public interest at the end of the project. He finally submits that the High Court Division overlooked that the project namely computerization of Examination Activities of Bangladesh Technical Education Board started for the period of 2(two) years from July, 2002 to June, 2004 and after completion of the project the petitioners sent proposal to the Ministry to absorb the respondent Nos. 1-3 but the Ministry refused and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. 
8. On the contrary the respondent Nos. 1-3 appearing in persons contended that there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division because the writ-respondent-petitioner appointed the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 with the condition that after the life time of the project their service will be transferred to the revenue setup. Clause 49 of the Project Profile contemplates that after the life time of the project the man-power of the computerization of the project will be transferred to revenue setup of the Board for the public interest and for continuing the computerization of examination activities in the Board. 
9. We have heard the learned Advocate for both the parties and perused the civil petition for leave to appeal, impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other materials on record. 
10. It appears that pursuant to notification dated 9-6-2004 (Annexure-A) upon recommendation of the Selection Committee (second) of the Bangladesh Technical Education Board-petitioner, the respondent Nos.1-3 were appointed as computer operators in the Project for Computerization of Examination Activities of Bangladesh Technical Education Board and the respondent No. 1 joined on 14-6-2004, the respondent No. 2 joined on 24-6-2004 and the respondent No. 3 joined on 12-6-2004 in their respective service for the period of the project. The terms and conditions of the appointment as per Memo dated 9-6-2004 reads as under:

আগারগাঁও, শেরে বাংলা নগর 
ঢাকা-১২০৭।

নিয়োগের শর্তাবলীঃ

11. On perusal of Annexure-B series it appears that at the end of the Project the respondent Nos. 1-3 were retained in their respective posts as Computer Operators on contractual basis for a period of 6(six) months in each time till June, 2009 vide letters dated 30-6-2005, 22-1-2006, 24-7-2006, 28-12-2006, 25-7-2007, 31-12-2007, 15-7-2008 and 22-1-2009 issued by the petitioner. Though the service of the respondent No. 2 on contractual basis was discontinued on 25-7-2007 yet he was verbally allowed to work on daily basis till June, 2009. Earlier Ministry of Establishment by its Memo dated 27-4-2005 (Annexure-1) rejected the proposal of the Ministry of Education vide Memo dated 29-3-2005 to transfer the 10 posts of the Computerization of the Project to the revenue budget. 
12. Considering the necessity of the service of the Computer Operators, the Bangladesh Inter-Education Boards Coordinating Sub-Committee in their 377th meeting dated 30-11-2006 (Annexure-K) discussed about regularization of the service of the Computer Operators in the created and existing vacant technical posts and the Chairman of the concerned Boards on principle agreed to the proposal. In the said meeting of the Bangladesh Inter-Education Boards Coordinating Sub-Committee adopted amongst others the following resolution: 
উল্লিখিত জাতীয় গুরুত্বপূর্ন ও সংবেদনশীল কাজের গুরুত্ব অনুধাবন করে কম্পিউটার কেন্দ্রের কার্যক্রম সুষ্ঠুভাবে পরিচালনার জন্য সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয় ও অর্থ মন্ত্রণালয়ের অনুমোদনক্রমে শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয় পত্র নং-শিম/শাঃ১০/পদ সৃষ্টি কম্পিঃকেন্দ্র-১/২০০০/৫৯৬, তারিখঃ ১-৯-২০০৫ইং এর মাধ্যমে শিক্ষা বোর্ড কম্পিউটার কেন্দ্রের ঢাকা, রাজশাহী, কুমিল্লা, যশোর, চট্টগ্রাম, বরিশাল, সিলেট ও বাংলাদেশ মাদরাসা বোর্ডের জন্য ১০২টি স্থায়ী পদ সৃজন করে। সৃজনকৃত ও পূর্বের শূন্য টেকনিক্যাল পদসমূহে শিক্ষা বোর্ড কম্পিউটার কেন্দ্রের সকল বোর্ডে বর্তমানে কর্মরত চুক্তিভিত্তিক ও মাস্টার রোল ভিত্তিক কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীদের স্থায়ীভাবে নিয়োগদানের ব্যাপারে এ কমিটির বিভিন্ন সভায় ব্যাপক আলোচনা হয়েছে। চুক্তিভিত্তিক ও মাস্টাররোল ভিত্তিক নিয়োজিত জনবলের কম্পিউটার কেন্দ্রের ফলাফল প্রক্রিয়াকরণ এবং কম্পিউটার ও এম.আর.মেশিন, প্রিন্টার ইত্যাদি সংক্রান্ত কাজে বিশেষভাবে দক্ষতা অর্জন করেছে ও বর্তমানে কর্মরত জনবল এ সমস্ত কাজে পারদর্শী। কাজেই শিক্ষা বোর্ড কম্পিউটার কেন্দ্রে বর্তমানে কর্মরত কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীদের উক্ত সৃজনকৃত শূন্য পদে নিয়োগ পাওয়ার অগ্রাধিকার রয়েছে এবং সে মোতাবেক বিভিন্ন সময়ে স্ব-স্ব বোর্ডের চেয়ারম্যান তাদের প্রতিশ্রুতিও প্রদান করেছেন।  
13. In the meeting of the Bangladesh Technical Education Board dated 8-1-2008 in respect of appointment of employees on contractual basis it has been acknowledged that against the 10 posts created in the Project for Computerization of Examination Activities of the Board 10 persons were appointed to the said posts in the Project after following required formalities and after the completion of the Project for smooth functioning of the Computerization of Examination Activities the employees appointed under the Project Profile were subsequently appointed on contractual basis. The Ministry of Establishment and the Ministry of Finance already approved the posts created by the Board under the development budget for the Computer Cell and it was expected that the final order by the Government would be issued immediately in this regard and in the circumstances it was decided to further appoint the employees on contractual basis in the Computer Cell who were earlier appointed on contractual basis. The relevant abstract from the minutes of the meeting of the aforesaid meeting dated 8-1-2008 is reproduced below: 
সিদ্ধান্তসমূহঃ
১।বোর্ডের পরীক্ষা পদ্ধতি কম্পিটারাইজেশন প্রকল্পের মাধ্যমে সৃষ্টিকৃত ১০টি পদের জনবল যথাযথ প্রক্রিয়ার মাধ্যমে প্রকল্পের আওতায় সৃষ্ট পদে নিয়োগ প্রদান করা হয়েছিল। প্রকল্পের মেয়াদ শেষ হওয়ার পর বোর্ডের পরীক্ষা পদ্ধতি কম্পিউটারাইজেশনের কাজ সচল রাখার জন্য প্রকল্পের মাধ্যমে নিয়োগকৃত জনবলকে চুক্তিভিত্তিক নিয়োগ প্রদান করে কার্যক্রম অব্যাহত রাখা হয়। 
বোর্ড কর্তৃক কম্পিউটার সেলের জন্য উন্নয়ন খাতে সৃষ্ট পদগুলো রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরের লক্ষ্যে ইতোমধ্যে সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয় ও অর্থ মন্ত্রণালয়ের অনুমোদন পাওয়া গিয়াছে। আশা করা যায় উক্ত পদগুলো রাজস্ব খাতে অচিরেই চূড়ান্ত জিও জারী হবে। এমতাবস্থায়, কম্পিউটার সেলের জন্য পূর্বে চুক্তিভিত্তিক নিয়োগকৃত কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারীদের চুক্তিভিত্তিক নিয়োগ প্রদান করা যেতে পারে।
14. From the above discussions, we find that apart from the stipulations made in clause 49 of the Project Profile to the effect that after the completion of the Project the manpower of the Computer Cell of the Project will be transferred to revenue budget of the Bangladesh Technical Education Board for the public interest, the petitioners in the meeting of the Board on 8-1-2008 decided to re-appoint the employees who were earlier appointed on contractual basis for smooth functioning of the Computerization of Examination Activities of the Board vide Memo dated 8-1-2008. In this context it is pertinent to quote clause 49 of the Project Profile which reads as under: 
"After the life time of the project the manpower (ten persons) of the computer cell of the project will be transferred to revenue budget of Bangladesh Technical Education Board for the public interest and for continuing of the computerization of examination activities in BTEB." 
15. Sanction for 9 posts of the Project for Computerization of Examination Activities of Bangladesh Technical Education Board was awarded on temporary basis by the Ministry of Education vide Memo dated 30-1-2008 (Annexure-C) with the approval of the Ministry of Establishment and the Ministry of Finance and out of 9 posts there were 4 (four) posts of Computer Operators along with 5(five) other posts and it was decided that the payment of the aforesaid posts will be made from revenue budget. 
16. It appears that the petitioner published recruitment notice vide Memo dated 6-7-2008 (Annexure-H) inviting applications amongst others for 3(three) posts of Computer Operators. Thereafter upon interview and recommendation of the Selection Committee one Md. Shahadat Hossain a computer operator of the Project was appointed in one out of 4(four) sanctioned posts and in other three posts, persons from outside the Project were appointed vide Memo dated 23-2-2010 (Annexure-E) but the respondents were left out of the appointment to the regular sanctioned revenue posts of Computer Operators. 
17. It appears that the notification issued vide SRO No. 182/Ain/2005/Shama/Bidhi-1 /S-9 /2000 dated 20-6-2005 published in Extraordinary Gazette concerning regularization and fixing seniority of the persons who have been transferred to the revenue setup from development project is not applicable to the writ petitioners because as per Rule 2(ka) these Rules are meant only for those development projects which started between 9th April, 1972 to 30th June, 1997. 
18. In the instant case before us the respondent Nos. 1-3 were appointed as Computer Operators under the Project for computerization of examination activities of the Bangladesh Technical Education Board pursuant to notification dated 9-6-2004. We have noticed that clause 49 of the Project Profile unequivocally provided that after the conclusion of the Project the manpower of the computer cell of the project will be transferred to the revenue budget of the Board. It is true that there is no provision for re-appointment of the manpower of the computer cell when a project is completed. But clause 49 provides for transfer of them to the revenue budget after the completion of the Project. It has been asserted on behalf of the petitioner that the Ministry of Establishment rejected the proposal of the Ministry of Education for transfer of the respondents' service to the revenue setup. But this does not improve the case of the petitioner in any way. Because the petitioner made representation to the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 that their service would be transferred to the revenue budget after completion of the project. 
19. The writ petitioners acted upon this representation to their detriment by not seeking other employment after completion of the project. Issuance of certificate of good performance in favour of the writ petitioners by the writ respondents [Annexures-F, F(1) and F(2)] together with their continuous appointment on contractual basis for a period of 6 months each time till June, 2009 gave high hope and created legitimate expectation among them that their job would be absorbed in the revenue setup. We have also seen that after completion of the Project the respondent Nos.1-3 were appointed as Computer Operators on contractual basis for smooth functioning of the Computerization of Examination Activities of Bangladesh Technical Education Board till June, 2009. We have seen that service of the respondent No. 2 though discontinued on 25-7-2007 yet he was verbally allowed to work on daily basis till June 2009. It also appears that the Ministry of Education vide Memo dated 30-1-2008 (Annexure-C) sanctioned 9(nine) posts of the Project for computerization of Examination Activities of Bangladesh Technical Education Board including 4(four) posts of Computer Operators of the Board on temporary basis with the approval of the Ministry of Establishment and the Ministry of Finance. But out of 4(four) sanctioned revenue posts of Computer Operators, only one person, Md Shahadat Hossain, a computer operator of the Project was appointed in the revenue budget and the respondent Nos. 1-3 were left out on the alleged ground that they failed to qualify themselves to be appointed under the revenue budget and, as such, they could not be appointed. 
20. From the facts of the case it appears that 3(three) posts are lying vacant but the service of the respondent Nos. 1-3 were not transferred under the revenue budget. As per clause 49 of the Project Profile respondent Nos. 1-3 made representation to the petitioner that after the completion of the Project their service should be transferred under the revenue budget without any examination for selection to those posts. The respondent Nos. 1-3 having relied on clause 49 joined in the service under the Project and had worked there till the completion of the Project and after completion of the Project the petitioner was obliged to appoint the respondent Nos. 1-3 under the revenue budget and, as such, the petitioners are estopped by the doctrine of promissory estoppel to appoint anyone other than the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 under the revenue budget. When a person makes a representation to any other person to do something and in reliance of which representation, the represent or changed his position to his detriment, the represent or cannot go back from his representation. This Court in a number of cases held that represented will be estopped by the doctrine of promissory estoppel to retract from going back from his commitment. 
21. The position of law is well settled that the Government shall be estopped from refusing any representation made by it on the basis of which any person has acted to his detriment, except that there is no estoppel against statute or there is no application of estoppel to prevent the performance any constitutional or statutory duty.
22. The doctrine of promissory estoppel was invoked by this Division in the case of Collector of Customs, Custom House, Chittagong vs A. Hannan reported in 42 DLR (AD) 167. In this case to avoid scarcity of sugar in the country the Government decided to import sugar under Wage Earners' Scheme and waived certain formalities. The Government issued notification reducing the existing customs duty and sales tax on the importation of sugar on fulfillment of certain conditions. The respondent availed this opportunity for importing sugar at the concessional rate of duty and sales tax fulfilling the conditions but before the arrival of the cargo and submission of the bill of entry the concessional rate was withdrawn by the Government. The Collector of Customs took view that the respondent was not entitled to concessional rate of customs duty and taxes because the bill of entry was delivered to the customs authority after the withdrawal of the concessional rate. This Division held that the importer having acted upon the assurance given, the Government cannot retrace its steps and ask for duty at the rate mentioned in the subsequent notification. 
23. The Supreme Court of India in the case of M/s. Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. Ltd. vs State of Uttar Pradesh, AIR 1979 (SC) 621 at page 644 observed as under: 
"But it is necessary to point out that since the doctrine of promissory estoppel is an equitable doctrine, it must yield when the equity so requires. If it can be shown by the Government that having regard to the facts as they have subsequently transpired, it would be inequitable to hold the Government to the promise made by it, the Court would not raise equity in favour of the promise and enforce the promise against the Government." 
24. In the instant case, by not appointing the respondents Nos.1-3 to the sanctioned posts of the computer operators, the petitioner has not served any public interest for which their action can be justified rather, as it is admitted fact that these respondents were appointed Computer Operators and gained technical knowledge and expertise from the service they rendered for a long time even after the life time of the project period, their non-appointment has caused much detriment to the public interest. 
25. Apart from the doctrine of promissory estoppels, doctrine of legitimate expectation is also applicable in the instant case. The doctrine of legitimate expectation contributed to the expansion of the duty to observe the requirements of natural justice by extending the duty beyond the relatively narrow range of rights and interests to which principles of natural justice had traditionally been applied. 
26. The legitimate expectation doctrine is invoked in a range of cases, the common theme of which was the principle that when administrative officials had created or induced a belief in a person about the possible exercise of their powers, any change affecting this belief should be conditioned by the rules of natural justice. The legitimate expectation doctrine provided important procedural benefits, namely, the right to be notified of, and to be heard in opposition to, the revocation of an existing benefit. The doctrine of legitimate expectation can be invoked broadly into four categories of cases. 
27. In the first category of cases a person acts upon relying on a generally applicable policy but the policy is subsequently changed to his disadvantage. The second category included cases in which a policy or norm of general application exists and continues but is not applied to the case of the person affecting him seriously. Third category arises when an individual is given a promise or a representation is made to him but which is not honoured due to a subsequent change to the policy. The fourth category of cases arise when an individual is given a promise or a representation is made to him which is subsequently dishonoured not for any change of policy but for the decision taken by the authority not to keep the promise. 
28. A substantive legitimate expectation is based on a promise or representation about an actual advantage or benefit. The Hong Kong Court of Appeal defined the substantive legitimate expectation doctrine in the following terms: 
"The doctrine recognizes that, in the absence of any overriding reason of law or policy excluding its operation, situations may arise in which persons may have a legitimate expectation of a substantive out-come or benefit, in which event failing to honour the expectation may, in particular circumstances, result in such unfairness to individuals as to amount to an abuse of power justifying intervention by the court." [Tung vs Director of Immigration (2002) 1 HKLRD 561, 600] 
29. The substantive legitimate expectation doctrine arises in two scenarios. The first is when a person who enjoys a benefit or a advantage argues that he expects that the benefit or advantage will continue. The other scenario is when a person has not yet enjoyed a benefit or advantage but argues that rightfully he expects that it will be granted. 
30. The protection of legitimate expectation is at the root of the principle of rule of law that requires that the government's dealings with public will be in a regular manner, predictable, certain, fair and not opposed to natural justice. In the case of Council of Civil Service Unions vs Minister for the Civil Service (1984) 3 All ER 935 House of Lords observed that for a legitimate expectation to arise in favour of a person the decision of the administrative authority must affect such person either (a) by altering rights or obligations of that person which are enforceable by or against him in private law or (b) by depriving him of some benefit or advantage which he has in the past been permitted by the decision maker to enjoy and which he can legitimately expect to be permitted to continue to do until some rational ground for withdrawing it has been communicated to him and he has been given an opportunity to comment thereon or he has received assurance from the decision-maker that they will not be withdrawn without first giving him an opportunity of advancing reasons for contending that they should not be withdrawn. 
31. This Division in the case of SSA Bangladesh Limited vs Engineer Mahmud-ul-Islam reported in 24 BLD (AD) 92 = 9 BLC (AD) 84 held as under: 
"60. The principle of legitimate expectation as enunciated in Schmidt vs Secretary of State of Home Affairs reported in (1969) I Ch. 140 imposed upon the Government or the concerned Authorities a duty to act fairly and reasonably in dealing with the rights and/or interest of the people and in case of any breach thereof the Court should act upon in striking down any order in exercise of judicial review of executive action and in case of any unreasonableness or inertness or even latches in its part for which some or part of which benefit is lost causing prejudice to the people at large, the Court may direct the concerned to exercise its functions fairly, reasonably and in accordance with law and established principles." 
32. The Supreme Court of India while explaining the nature and scope of the doctrine of legitimate expectation in the case of Food Corporation of India vs M/s Kamdhenu Cattle Feed Industries (1993) 1 SCC 71 at page 76, paragraph 8 observed as under: 
"The mere reasonable or legitimate expectation of a citizen, in such a situation, may not by itself be a distinct enforceable right, but failure to consider and give due weight to it may render the decision arbitrary, and this is how the requirement of due consideration of a legitimate expectation forms part of the principle of non-arbitrariness, a necessary concomitant of the rule of law. Every legitimate expectation is a relevant factor requiring due consideration in a fair decision making process. Whether the expectation of the claimant is reasonable or legitimate in the context is a question of fact in each case. Whenever the question arises, it is to be determined not according to the claimant's perception but in larger public interest wherein other more important considerations may outweigh what would otherwise have been the legitimate expectation of the claimant. A bonafide decision of the public authority reached in this manner would satisfy the requirement of non-arbitrariness and withstand judicial scrutiny. The doctrine of legitimate expectation gets assimilated in the rule of law and operates in our legal system in this manner and to this extent." 
33. In the case of Sethi Auto Service Station vs Delhi Development Authority, 2009 (1) SCC 180 DK Jain, J observed: 
"32 A case for applicability of the doctrine of legitimate expectation, now accepted in the subjective sense as part of our legal jurisprudence, arises when an administrative body by reason of a representation or by past practice or conduct aroused an expectation which it would be within its powers to fulfill unless some overriding public interest comes in the way. However, a person who bases his claim on the doctrine of legitimate expectation, in the first instance, has to satisfy that he has relied on the said representation and the denial of that expectation has worked to his detriment. The Court could interfere only if the decision taken by the authority was found to be arbitrary, unreasonable or in gross abuse of power or in violation of principles of natural justice and not taken in public interest. But a claim based on mere legitimate expectation without anything more cannot ipso facto give a right to invoke these principles." 
34. The present respondent as writ petitioners laid a foundation in the petition that they were appointed in the Project with an understanding that after the life time of the Project their service will be transferred to the revenue budget of Bangladesh Technical Education Board for the public interest and continuing of the Computerization of Examination Activities of Bangladesh Technical Education Board pursuant to clause 49 of the Project Profile. Thereby the writ petitioners successfully made out a case of their service to be transferred to the revenue setup on the doctrine of legitimate expectation. From a plain reading of clause 49 of the Project Profile it is evident that Bangladesh Technical Education Board made a representation to the writ petitioners that after the completion of Project their service would be transferred to revenue budget of Bangladesh Technical Education Board. Thus the writ petitioners were assured that they would be regularized in the revenue setup after the completion of the Project. In the instant case the writ petitioners having requisite qualifications appeared before the competent Selection Committee who after proper examination through a competitive examination among the prospective candidates found the writ petitioners to be competent and qualified and appointed them in the Project. After the life time of the Project the writ petitioners were not transferred to the revenue setup pursuant to clause 49 of the Project Profile. For the reason best known to the writ respondent No. 1 petitioner at the end of the Project the writ petitioners were allowed to retain in their respective posts as Computer Operators on contractual basis till June 2009 after completion of the project. It has been noticed that the writ respondent No. 1-petitioner made representation/commitment that they will be appointed to their posts on regular basis in the revenue setup of the Government as soon as sanction for the said posts is obtained from the Government. On perusal of the Annexure B series it appears that the writ petitioners-respondent Nos. 1 to 3 were appointed on temporary basis for a period of six months and their services were renewed after the expiry of every six months till 22-1-2009. It is true that the writ petitioners after completion of the Project continued their service on contractual basis and they also faced interview for direct appointment in those posts but failed to succeed in the interview. Since the writ petitioners were assured that pursuant to clause 49 of the Project Profile after life time of the Project their service would be transferred to the revenue budget rather their service were continued on contractual basis till 2009. The writ petitioners-respondent Nos. 1 to 3 in a compelling circumstance having no other alternative continued their service on contractual basis after completion of their Project and thereby they cannot be termed to have waved their right of being absorbed in the revenue setup under the Government. 
35. It also appears that the respondent Nos. 1-3 successfully completed 5(five) years of their service to the Board with dedication and sincerity. It is their legitimate expectation that after the completion of the Project their service will be transferred to the revenue setup pursuant to clause 49 of the Project Profile. We find that the High Court Division rightly found that the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 having appeared before the Interview Board for direct appointment to the post of Computer Operators of the Board have not waved their right to be transferred to the revenue setup of the Board. From Annexure-B series of the writ petition we find that the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 continued in their service till June, 2005 on the basis of their earlier appointment and that the Project ended on 30-6-2005. Therefore, the respondent Nos. 1-3 were legally entitled to have their service transferred to the revenue budget of the Board on and from 1-7-2005. We do not find any merit in the submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner. 
36. In the above facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the High Court Division having considered all the materials on record and the submissions advanced on behalf of both the parties arrived at a correct decision in making the Rule absolute with a direction upon the petitioner-Board to transfer the respondents' service as Computer Operators to the revenue budget with effect from 1-7-2005 within 2(two) months from the date of receipt of the judgment. However, the writ-petitioners-respondents would not get any extra salary for the period they served on contractual basis which does not require any interference by this Division. 
Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed. 
End.
